Download the data

Source: vignettes/articles/data.Rmd
data.Rmd

The reference tables and journal-level aggregates are published as Parquet files with every release. They are kept in the parquet/ folder of the repository and can be read without an account or API key, in R, Python, DuckDB or any other tool that reads Parquet. Article-level tables (articles, article_first_authors, article_agreements) are only in BigQuery, subugoe-collaborative.jn_analytics.

Data and code are released under CC0.

Every table and column is described in the data model, including the counting rules. Two matter most when working with the files:

  • Counts can be summed over journals, years and work types; compute shares from the sums. Filter work_type to article and review for research articles.
  • The country tables count a work once per first-author country (full counting). Take totals from journal_year, never by summing over countries.

Usage

R, with jnanalytics

Download all files into one folder and use the analysis functions:

library(jnanalytics)

base_url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/"
files <- paste0(c(jn_publish_tables(), "release"), ".parquet")
dir.create("jn_parquet")
for (f in files) {
  download.file(paste0(base_url, f), file.path("jn_parquet", f), mode = "wb")
}

src <- jn_source("jn_parquet")
jn_oa(src, by = c("pub_year", "oa_model"))

R, with arrow 

download.file(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/journal_year.parquet",
  "journal_year.parquet", mode = "wb"
)
journal_year <- arrow::read_parquet("journal_year.parquet")

Python 

import pandas as pd

url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/journal_year.parquet"
journal_year = pd.read_parquet(url)

DuckDB

DuckDB reads the files directly from their URL:

SELECT pub_year, oa_model,
       sum(articles) AS articles,
       sum(articles_oa) / sum(articles) AS share_oa
FROM 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/njahn82/jn_analytics/main/parquet/journal_year.parquet'
WHERE work_type IN ('article', 'review')
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY ALL;

Column descriptions in the files

Each file carries its column descriptions as JSON in the Parquet metadata (jn_columns), together with the table name (jn_table) and the package version (jn_version):

meta <- arrow::open_dataset("journal_year.parquet")$schema$metadata
jsonlite::fromJSON(meta$jn_columns)
